extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraic geometers, mathematicians writing scripts using schubert.lib, swalk.lib, tropicalNewton.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (schubert.lib, swalk.lib, tropicalNewton.lib) describing usage, inputs, outputs, assumptions, theory/purpose and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: addSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: addSheaf(A,B); A sheaf, B sheaf. Return: sheaf. Theory: This is the direct sum of two sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows creating subBundle and quotientBundle on Grassmannian and adding them: 'sheaf D = S + Q;'. Also cross-references dualSheaf, quotSheaf, symmetricPowerSheaf, tensorSheaf. Example verifies Chern character and total Chern class equal 1 in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeGraphVE
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume: v is a list of vertices, e is a list of edges. Return: graph with vertices v and edges e. Theory: Creates a graph from a list of vertices and edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage example shows calling makeGraphVE and printing: 'A graph with 2 vertices and 1 edges'. Input format illustrated: lists of vertex descriptors and edge lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: printGraphG
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: printGraphG(G); G graph. Assume: G is a graph. Theory: This is the print function used by Singular to print a graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates print output of a graph created by makeGraphVE. No extra return value documented (print-only).

rubrics_metrics.name: moduliSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: moduliSpace(V,d); V variety, d int. Assume: V is a projective space and d is a positive integer. Return: (implied) stack (a moduli space). Theory: Function used by Singular to create a moduli space of stable maps from a genus zero curve to a projective space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'stack M = moduliSpace(P,2);' prints 'A moduli space of dimension 11'. Cross-references other stack-related functions (printStack, dimStack, fixedPoints).

rubrics_metrics.name: printStack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: printStack(M); M stack. Assume: M is a moduli space of stable maps. Theory: This is the print function used by Singular to print a stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printing a moduli space created by moduliSpace(P,2) and output 'A moduli space of dimension 11'.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimStack
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dimStack(M); M stack. Return: int. Input: M is a moduli space of stable maps. Output: the dimension of moduli space of stable maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling dimStack(M) returns 11 for M = moduliSpace(P,2).

rubrics_metrics.name: fixedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fixedPoints(M); M stack. Return: list. Input: M is a moduli space of stable maps. Output: a list of graphs corresponding the fixed point components of a torus action on a moduli space of stable maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example checks size(F) = 100 and types of elements: F[1] is a list, F[1][1] is a graph, F[1][2] is an int. Cross-reference contributionBundle and normalBundle which operate on these fixed components.

rubrics_metrics.name: contributionBundle
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: contributionBundle(M,G,#); M stack, G graph, # list. Return: number. Input: M is a moduli space of stable maps, G is a graph, # is a list. Output: a number corresponding to the contribution bundle on a moduli space of stable maps at a fixed point component (graph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: contributionBundle(M,G) and contributionBundle(M,G,5) produce same numeric result in example (f == g → 1). Cross-reference normalBundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalBundle
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: number. Input: M is a moduli space of stable maps, G is a graph. Output: a number corresponding to the normal bundle on a moduli space of stable maps at a graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example checks normalBundle(M,G) is nonzero. Cross-reference contributionBundle. (The 'Theory' and 'hypersurfaces' text around this entry indicates use in fixed point computations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: multipleCover
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multipleCover(d); d int. Return: number. Theory: This is the contribution of degree d multiple covers of a smooth rational curve as a Gromov-Witten invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for d=1..6 showing numeric outputs (1, 1/8, 1/27, ...). Cross-references linesHypersurface and rationalCurve.

rubrics_metrics.name: linesHypersurface
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: linesHypersurface(n); n int. Return: number. Theory: This is the number of lines on a general hypersurface of degree d = 2n-3 in an n-dimensional projective space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples list values for n=2..9 and warn of int overflow for large n (many // ** int overflow(^), result may be wrong messages). Cross-references multipleCover and rationalCurve.

rubrics_metrics.name: rationalCurve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rationalCurve(d,#); d int, # list. Return: number. Theory: This is the Gromov-Witten invariant corresponding the number of rational curves on a general Calabi-Yau threefold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rationalCurve(1) → 2875. Many commented-out example calls illustrate optional list arguments specifying partition types for insertions. Cross-references linesHypersurface and multipleCover.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumofquotients
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sumofquotient(M,F,#); M stack, F list, # list. Return: number. Theory: This is useful for the parallel computation of rationalCurve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sumofquotients(M,F) returns 4876875/8 for a particular moduli space and fixedPoints list; also accepts an optional list argument. Designed for aggregating contributions from fixed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: homog_part
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homog_part(f,n); f poly, n int. Return: poly. Purpose: computing the homogeneous component of a polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate extracting homogeneous components of various degrees from a sample polynomial. Useful when working in weighted projective rings (example uses wp(1,2,3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: homog_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homog_parts(f,i,j); f poly, i int, j int. Return: poly. Theory: computing a polynomial which is the sum of the homogeneous components of a polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows homog_parts(f,2,4) returns sum of degree 2 through 4 components. Works with weighted projective rings as in example.

rubrics_metrics.name: logg
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: logg(f,n); f poly, n int. Return: poly. Theory: computing Chern characters from total Chern classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: logg(1+x+y,4) returns series expression representing Chern characters. Intended for Chern class / Chern character conversions in Schubert computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: expp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: expp(f,n); f poly, n int. Return: poly. Purpose: computing total Chern classes from Chern characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: expp(3+x,3) returns total Chern class polynomial 1/6x3+1/2x2+x+1. Complementary to logg.

rubrics_metrics.name: SchubertClass
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: SchubertClass(p); p list (a list of integers which is a partition). Return: poly. Purpose: compute the Schubert classes on a Grassmannian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: on Grassmannian(2,4) with p = [1,1], SchubertClass(p) → q(1)^2-q(2). Cross-reference dualPartition.

rubrics_metrics.name: dualPartition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dualPartition(k,n,p); k int, n int, p list. Return: list. Purpose: compute the dual of a partition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dualPartition(2,4,list(2,1)) illustrated. See also SchubertClass. Output format is a list (example shows small printed lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: swalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: swalk(i[,v,w]); i ideal, v,w int vectors. Description: The sagbi basis of the subalgebra defined by the generators of i, calculated via the Sagbi walk algorithm from the ordering dp to lp if v,w are not given (resp. from the ordering (a(v),lp) to the ordering (a(w),lp) if v and w are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: (implicit) printed list of generators forming the sagbi basis. Example shows invocation on an ideal and the printed basis elements. Reference to SAGBI theory and related grwalk and rwalk libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: rswalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rswalk(i,weight rad,p deg[,v,w]); i ideal, v,w int vectors. Description: The sagbi basis of the subalgebra defined by the generators of i, calculated via the Sagbi walk algorithm from the ordering dp to lp if v,w are not given (resp. from the ordering (a(v),lp) to the ordering (a(w),lp) if v and w are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows rswalk(I,2,2) producing the same printed sagbi basis as swalk for the example ideal. Parameters weight, rad, p, deg control internal algorithm behavior (not fully spelled out in the chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: setUniformizingParameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: setUniformizingParameter(p); p number. Return: none, sets the uniformizing parameter as p. Assume: char(K)==0 and p prime number or trdeg(K)>0 and p transcendental variable or p==0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage for 'poor man's polynomials over Puiseux series' (ring r = (0,t),x,dp; setUniformizingParameter(t)) and for p-adic like examples (setUniformizingParameter(2)). Must export or set a global uniformizingParameter for other tropicalNewton routines to work.

rubrics_metrics.name: val
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: val(c); c number. Return: int, the valuation of an element in the ground field. Assume: uniformizingParameter is set and c!=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: val(t2+t3) → 2 when t is uniformizing parameter for Puiseux-like ring; val(12) → 2 when uniformizingParameter=2 for p-adic like example. Used in tropical computations to extract valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonPolygonNegSlopes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: newtonPolygonNegSlopes(g,b); g poly, b int. Return: list, the negative slopes of the Newton Polygon of g. If b==1, computes root (type poly) instead if (easily) possible. Assume: uniformizingParameter is set and g univariate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing slopes for small polynomials in Puiseux and p-adic style rings. Useful as a step in Newton polygon based tropical/root computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: cccMatrixToPositiveIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cccMatrixToPositiveIntvec(M); M matrix. Return: intvec, strictly positive equivalent as weight vector to row vector in M. Assume: constant coefficient case only, will scale weight vector and add vectors of ones to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates converting an integer matrix of valuations to a strictly positive integer weight vector and using it for computing an initial ideal via switchRingsAndComputeInitialIdeal. Shows interaction with tropicalPointNewton output and switchRingsAndComputeInitialIdeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalPointNewton
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalPointsLasVegas(I); I ideal. Return: matrix, a matrix containing a tropical point as row vector. Assume: uniformizingParameter is set and I monomial free. Note: if printlevel sufficiently high will print intermediate data and timings; returns error if randomly chosen hyperplanes are not generic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show setting uniformizingParameter, running tropicalPointNewton(I) and printing intermediate steps when printlevel=3 (maximal independent set, substitutions, Newton polygon analysis, timing). Output is a row vector of valuations used for subsequent steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: switchRingsAndComputeInitialIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: switchRingsAndComputeInitialIdeal(I,w); I ideal, w intvec. Return: ring, a ring containing the initial ideal with respect to w. Assume: constant coefficient case and w strictly positive integer. Note: if printlevel sufficiently high will print timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows converting tropicalPointNewton output into a positive integer weight vector and then calling this procedure to compute an initial ideal; prints timing and requires uniformizingParameter handling. Intended for use in tropical Newton pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalVarietyNewton
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalVarietyNewton(I); I ideal. Return: matrix, a matrix containing all elements of the tropical variety. Assume: uniformizingParameter is set, I monomial free and zero-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example computes tropical variety for a zero-dimensional ideal and iterates to print each integer vector in the tropical variety. Requires uniformizingParameter in environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalLinkNewton
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalLinkNewton(inI); inI ideal. Return: matrix, a matrix containing generators of all rays of the tropical variety. Assume: constant coefficient case, inI is monomial free, its tropical variety has codimension one lineality space and is a polyhedral fan. Note: if printlevel sufficiently high will print intermediate results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates a complex usage computing a 10-valent facet in tropical Grass(3,7) with a large ideal in a weighted polynomial ring; shows that the routine prints intermediate steps when verbose and expects careful setup of ring and uniformizingParameter.
